newsitem.title: FRANCE: Boutros-Ghali sees Chirac on Middle East, Africa.
newsitem.headline: Boutros-Ghali sees Chirac on Middle East, Africa.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali met Jacques Chirac on Wednesday and said the French president was very worried by the faltering Middle East peace process days before a trip to the region.
Boutros-Ghali, visiting Chirac at the Elysee presidential palace, discussed both the Middle East and Africa during a one-hour meeting, French officials said.
The U.N. chief, who has French backing for a new term that the United States has vowed to veto, told reporters that "the problems of the Middle East worry him a great deal."
Chirac is to leave on Saturday for a trip to Syria, Israel, Palestinian territories, Jordan, Lebanon and Egypt as part of a French push for a greater role in Middle East peacekeeping.
French officials said the two men also discussed how to follow up pledges to help Africa. The pledges were made at a summit of the seven main industrial democracies in Lyon, central France, in June.

Boutros-Ghali also met Foreign Minister Herve de Charette on Tuesday evening in Paris. He leaves Paris on Wednesday to go to Hamburg in Germany for talks ahead of the inauguration of the U.N. Law of the Sea tribunal on Friday.
